record.paper_title: SOFT PHYSICS AND INTERMITTENCY : OPEN QUESTION(S) in KRAKOW
record.original_question: Why do simulations of hadron-induced reactions fail to reproduce the observed low-multiplicity and P_T behavior of fluctuations, unlike simulations for lepton-induced reactions, and can resolving this discrepancy clarify the soft component of the intermittency problem?

evidence.quote: 3. The "multiplicity and PT " problem. In hadron-induced reactions, it has been noticed[14] that, in contradiction with lepton-induced reactions, simulations are far from reproducing the low multiplicity and PT behaviour of fluctuations.
As such this remains an unexplained feature which, if a solution is found, can open some doors for the "soft" part of the intermittency problem.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the phenomenon of intermittency in high-energy multiparticle production, defined as the power-law growth of scaled factorial moments of charged-particle multiplicity distributions as the size of the phase-space cell (in rapidity, azimuthal angle, and/or transverse momentum p_T) decreases. Empirically, in lepton-induced reactions (e.g., e+e- and lepton-hadron scattering), Monte Carlo simulations based on parton cascades plus standard hadronization successfully reproduce the observed behavior of the factorial moments, including their dependence on event multiplicity and on the transverse-momentum window used to define the phase-space cells. In hadron-induced reactions, by contrast, the same families of simulations fail to reproduce the observed dependence of the factorial moments on the multiplicity of the event and on p_T, particularly in the low-multiplicity and low-p_T regimes, where the "soft" (non-perturbative) component of multiparticle production dominates.

Provide a dynamical explanation for the following two coupled questions:

(a) Identify the mechanism in hadron-induced collisions—absent or different from that in lepton-induced collisions—that causes simulations to underestimate or otherwise misdescribe the low-multiplicity and low-p_T behavior of the scaled factorial moments. The explanation should specify the soft-physics ingredient (e.g., a property of the underlying non-perturbative cascade, the rôle of strings/clusters, beam-remnant correlations, or another mechanism) responsible for the discrepancy.

(b) Show that, once this mechanism is identified and incorporated, the resulting model accounts quantitatively for both the multiplicity dependence and the p_T dependence of the factorial moments observed in hadron-induced reactions, and discuss to what extent this resolution clarifies the soft component of the intermittency problem.
artifact.status_search_result: Literature on intermittency in hadron-induced collisions confirms that soft, non-perturbative multiparticle production remains incompletely modeled and that simulations have difficulty reproducing factorial-moment behavior at low multiplicity and low p_T. No clear, widely accepted resolution explaining the multiplicity/p_T discrepancy between hadron- and lepton-induced reactions was found; the problem appears to remain open or only partially addressed by subsequent model improvements (e.g., EPOS, AMPT studies).

status_evidence.claim: Recent simulations continue to investigate intermittency at low p_T, indicating the issue remains under active study.

status_evidence.title: Scaling properties of multiplicity fluctuations in heavy-ion collisions simulated by AMPT model
status_evidence.snippet: Multiplicity fluctuations in hadronic cascade simulations.
status_evidence.claim: Ongoing modeling work suggests the multiplicity/p_T problem in soft intermittency has not been definitively resolved.

status_evidence.title: Convolutions, factorial cumulants and intermittency
status_evidence.claim: Theoretical work continues on the structure of factorial moments without a closed resolution of the hadron vs. lepton discrepancy.
